chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleyman ibn Dawood Al-Minqari, who said: An-Nadr ibn Ismail Al-Balkhi informed me, from Abu Hamza Al-Thumali, from Shahr ibn Howshab.

He said: Al-Hajjaj said to me and asked me about the Prophet's (peace be upon him and his family) going out to his battlefields, so I said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) participated in Badr with three hundred and thirteen, and participated in Uhud with six hundred, and participated in Al-Khandaq (The Trench) with nine hundred.
He said: From whom are you saying this? I said: From Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said: Strayed is the one, by Allah, who walks upon other than his way.

key_terms.جَعْفَرُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ: Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), the sixth Imam

ai.seo_question: What did Al-Hajjaj say about those who follow a path other than the Prophet's way?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the transmission of historical data regarding the Prophet's battles through the Ahl al-Bayt, specifically citing Ja'far al-Sadiq as the authoritative source for Shahr ibn Howshab. Al-Hajjaj’s response, 'By God, whoever follows a path other than his is astray,' underscores the Shia doctrine of the infallibility and exclusive guidance of the Imams, contrasting their lineage-based knowledge with the caliphal or Umayyad perspective. This narrative serves as a foundational proof for the reliability of hadith chains originating from the Imams in Shia scholarship.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Suleyman Bin Dawood Al Minqary, from Ismail Al Balkhy, from Abu Hamza Al Sumaly, from Shahr Bin Howshab who said,

‘Al-Hajjaj said to me and asked me about the going out of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> to his<sup>saww</sup> overseeing it (the battles), so I said, ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> oversaw (the battle of) Badr among three hundred and thirteen (combatants), and oversaw (the battle of) Ohad among six hundred (combatants), and oversaw (the battle of) Khandaq among nine hundred (combatants)’.

He said, ‘From whom are you saying it, from Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> Bin Muhammad<sup>asws</sup>?’ So I said, ‘Strayed is the one, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, who walks upon other than his<sup>asws</sup> way’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from and Ali ibn Muhammad from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulayman al-Minqariy who has said that narrated to him al-Nadr ibn Isma’il al-Balkhiy from abu Hamzah al-Thumaliy from Shahr ibn Hawshab who has said the following:

“Al-Hajjaj asked me about the Messenger of Allah’s mobilization for the wars in which he, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, took part. I said, ‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, mobilized for Badr with three hundred and thirteen people. He mobilized for Uhud with six hundred and for al-Khandaq (Battle of Ditches) with nine hundred people.’
He asked, ‘Who has said it?’ I replied, ‘Ja’far ibn Muhammad, ‘Alayhi al-Salam .’ He then said, ‘By Allah whoever adopts a way other than his way is lost.’”
